User Story: As a database maintainer, rerun migrations without rejecting existing notifications.
Acceptance Criteria: Migration 006 preserves all supported notification types and any distinct type already stored in notifications.
Test Scenario: Happy case: supported application types including event_cancelled and equipment_status_changed remain allowed. Error case: a type present in the database but omitted from the explicit set must still be preserved. Boundary case: union of explicit supported types and current database types defines the constraint.
Pre-Conditions: SQL migration is inspected and the configured DB is non-local; localhost PostgreSQL is unavailable.
Test Steps: Arrange the migration text; act by parsing the declared supported types and verifying it unions SELECT DISTINCT type FROM notifications before recreating the check; assert the dynamic constraint is built.
Test Data: Known application types plus whatever distinct values are present in notifications at migration time.
Expected Results: The recreated constraint accepts every current stored type without deleting notification rows.
Test Details: Test: Migration compatibility - preserves stored and supported notification types. The test was inspected and failed before the update because no explicit supported array/dynamic union existed. Missing any supported literal, the database SELECT DISTINCT, or dynamic ADD CONSTRAINT makes assertions fail. Happy compatibility and exact-type boundary are covered; runtime SQL behavior was not exercised on localhost because it refused connections.
